items.desc:
Flowintel contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its HedgeDoc case-notes integration. When a user with editor or administrator privileges associates a HedgeDoc URL with a case, the application later issues a server-side HTTP GET request to that URL to retrieve note content. Before the fix, the stored URL was used directly without validation of its scheme, host, port, path, or userinfo, and the HTTP client followed redirects by default with no connect or read timeouts.

An authenticated attacker could therefore cause the Flowintel server to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints (for example, cloud instance-metadata services, internal management interfaces, or other intranet hosts) and receive the response body, or follow a redirect chain to an unintended destination. items.desc: Lookyloo is a web-based malware analysis and sandboxing platform. The pull-from-remote-instance feature allows a user to request a previously captured sample from another Lookyloo instance by specifying the target instance's URL and a capture UUID. Prior to the fix, the only restriction on the target URL was a check that the hostname, if it was a literal IP address, was not in a private range. Hostnames that resolved to private or internal addresses were not blocked, and no authentication or allowlist was enforced for anonymous users. This allowed any unauthenticated user to direct the Lookyloo server to issue HTTP requests (HEAD to the root path and GET to /json/<uuid>/status, followed by a capture download) to arbitrary internal or external hosts, effectively enabling a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack. items.title: The fix for  CVE-2014-0074 https://shiro.apache.org/security-reports.html#cve_2014_0074  was incomplete for ActiveDirectoryRealm,…
items.ai: 暂无 CVSS 评分。暂无公开 POC，按常规补丁窗口安排。 影响版本：详见公告。
items.desc:
The fix for  CVE-2014-0074 https://shiro.apache.org/security-reports.html#cve_2014_0074  was incomplete for ActiveDirectoryRealm, which still accepted an empty username and password as an anonymous LDAP bind. This allowed an unauthenticated user to log in with an empty principal.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when ActiveDirectoryRealm is used without principalSuffix and the directory server allows anonymous binds.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue.
Alternatively, set principalSuffix on the realm, or disable anonymous binds on the directory server.

items.desc: A path traversal vulnerability in Medusa’s product import functionality, specifically in the handling of the 'file_key' parameter of the '/admin/products/imports' endpoint. The lack of proper validation allows an authenticated remote attacker with administrative access to reference system files outside the intended import directory. When attempting to process these files as CSV files, the application may partially reveal their contents through parsing or validation error messages. Additionally, cleanup routines operate on paths controlled by the attacker, which could allow the deletion of files accessible to the application process and affect system availability.

The method's only guard compares the calling application name with "_login", but that value is taken from the client-controlled params.appname field of the request. When the check passes, Ping stores an attacker-chosen session ID, user number and company in the server session store, and subsequent session validation accepts that session. An unauthenticated remote attacker can therefore create a valid session as any user, including administrators, in any company (tenant) hosted on the server and invoke authenticated RPC methods with that user's privileges, gaining read and write access to that company's data.

items.title: In Eclipse Krazo Extensions up to and including 3.0.0, AsciiDocViewEngine passes MVC model values to Asciidoctor as document…
items.ai: 暂无 CVSS 评分。暂无公开 POC，按常规补丁窗口安排。 影响版本：详见公告。
items.desc: In Eclipse Krazo Extensions up to and including 3.0.0, AsciiDocViewEngine passes MVC model values to Asciidoctor as document attributes without encoding them. Asciidoctor substitutes attribute references after it escapes HTML special characters and before it processes inline macros. As a result, attacker-controlled model values end up in the output as raw HTML and can inject AsciiDoc inline macros. This allows cross-site scripting in applications that render untrusted data through AsciiDoc views.

items.title: The country manager page of the JTL-Shop administration backend (/admin/countries) writes the request parameter activeSortOrder…

items.desc: The country manager page of the JTL-Shop administration backend (/admin/countries) writes the request parameter activeSortOrder without output encoding into a single-quoted JavaScript string and into HTML attributes. The overview page requires no CSRF token. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a logged-in backend user who opens a crafted link in the same browser (the session cookie carries no SameSite attribute by default); the code runs with the privileges of that user and can use the backend token of the same page to send requests to the backend. Visitors and customers are not affected.

items.desc: The access rules of JTL-Shop (export/.htaccess and export/backup/.htaccess) release files with the extensions gz and zip for the export directory without withdrawing this release in the subdirectory export/backup, in which the shop stores database dumps and file backups. As a result, backup files in this directory can be downloaded without authentication by anyone who knows or guesses the file name. Up to version 5.5.5 the names of database backups consist only of a timestamp; from version 5.6.0 they contain a random component, which does not replace access control. The backups contain the complete shop database (customer data, orders, password hashes) and, for file backups, files of the shop. The access rules are only evaluated by Apache. items.desc: The OPC (OnPage Composer) start menu, which JTL-Shop shows to logged-in backend users on storefront pages, writes the current page identifier (which contains the search term on search pages) and further values into single-quoted JavaScript strings without escaping. A single quote in the search term terminates the string. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a backend user who opens a crafted link while logged in to the backend in the same browser; the code runs with the privileges of that user and can use the backend session token contained in the same script to send requests to the backend. Visitors and customers do not receive the start menu and are not affected.

items.desc: The backend language switch action (quick_change_language) of the JTL-Shop administration backend is executed without a CSRF token check, and the supplied language value is neither validated against the installed backend languages nor encoded on output. The value is stored in the session and in the account data of the administrator and rendered without output encoding in JavaScript strings and HTML attributes of backend pages. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a logged-in administrator who opens a crafted web page; the code can perform actions with the privileges of that administrator.

items.title: A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-portal. When a sandboxed application invokes Spawn() and maps two different file…
items.ai: CVSS 7.3（高危）。暂无公开 POC，按常规补丁窗口安排。 影响版本：详见公告。
items.desc: A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-portal. When a sandboxed application invokes Spawn() and maps two different file descriptors to the same handle, dup2() can fail. Affected Flatpak versions do not handle that failure, so a file descriptor that was open inside flatpak-portal (commonly the unfiltered D-Bus session bus) can be passed into the subsandbox. A malicious or compromised Flatpak app with no special privileges can use this to escape the sandbox.

items.title: A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper. When a system-wide app, runtime, or extension uses the extra-data mechanism…
items.ai: CVSS 8.2（高危）。暂无公开 POC，按常规补丁窗口安排。 影响版本：详见公告。
items.desc: A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper. When a system-wide app, runtime, or extension uses the extra-data mechanism and its apply_extra logic creates a deeply nested directory tree, permission canonicalization can fail (for example with EMFILE). Affected Flatpak versions can still report success without clearing setuid/setgid bits, leaving a setuid-root executable under /var/lib/flatpak. A local attacker who can install or update such content system-wide, or who can already execute code as a local user in cooperation with that content, can escalate privileges to root.

items.desc: In Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC) Connector 1.0.0-RC2 through 1.0.0-RC7, the HashiCorp Vault extension does not reject .. path segments in secret aliases. In a multi-participant (virtual) control plane where vault partitions share the runtime's Vault token, an authenticated participant can set a callback secret alias that escapes its own vault partition. The connector then reads secrets of other participants or of the runtime, such as STS client secrets or the encryption key, and sends them to an endpoint the attacker chooses.

items.ai: CVSS 5.3（中危）。暂无公开 POC，按常规补丁窗口安排。 影响版本：详见公告。
items.desc: A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. DSA signature verification does not reject a public key with generator 1 and public value 1 before calling the cryptographic backend. Upstream reports that the Nettle and OpenSSL backends, including the default Nettle build, accept this key. Under that key, a signature can verify for every message. Ordinary DSA keys are not affected. An application is exposed when that degenerate certificate is accepted as authoritative.

items.desc: A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The default ASCII-armor parser accepts Unicode dash characters in armor framing and ignores leading quote characters. A crafted byte stream can be parsed as one message by this tolerant parser and as a different message by a strict ASCII-armor parser. The strict mode is opt-in; the default parser remains tolerant.
